note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after bb173975ea). Read at rfc/full/rfc7950.txt Section 7.2.2: "A submodule MUST only be included by either the module to which it belongs or another submodule that belongs to that module." Producer: checkStructure (joined by Resolve) runs moduleIncludeErrors over every loaded module and submodule (sourceModules); it resolves the including unit's owner (its own name, or its belongs-to) and refuses an include whose submodule belongs to another module with ErrIncludeBelongsTo. TestRFC7950SubmoduleIncludedOnlyByItsModule covers both clauses in both polarities: negatives refuse module a including s (belongs-to b) and submodule a-s of a including s, each requiring the text "belongs to module b"; positives load module a including a-t and a-s including sibling a-t. Module b is loaded and includes s in the negatives, so only the belongs-to differs. Independent overlay mutants (tags ze_core ze_bgp), each red on an assertion: owner ignores belongs-to (submodule-sibling positive red), modules skipped (submodule negative red), submodules skipped (module negative red), comparison always passes (both negatives red), comparison always fails (both positives red). Two equivalent-in-test mutants survive: dropping either lookup in includedSubmodule (include.Module, or the SubModules map fallback) leaves the test green because the other still finds the submodule; the redundancy changes no verdict but no test proves the fallback is needed. The recorded revert tuples (panic in moduleIncludeErrors) prove reach only. {gap} removed from the row in bb173975ea; Ze ships no submodule of its own, so the check guards loaded module sets.
